query: What is reciprocal rank fusion and when is it used?
report:
## Summary

Reciprocal rank fusion combines several ranked lists into one by summing reciprocal ranks rather than comparing raw scores, and it is the standard way to merge lexical and dense retrieval [1].

## Where it is used

The TREC Retrieval-Augmented Generation track evaluates systems that fuse multiple retrievers this way [3]. The same arXiv paper is also mirrored at version 3 of its listing [2].

citations.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
citations.content: Combining parametric memory with non-parametric memory through retrieval has become a common approach to knowledge-intensive tasks. Rank fusion is the standard way to merge a lexical and a dense ranked list, because raw scores from the two are not on a comparable scale.
